scenes.text: High in the Himalayas, there's a lake full of human skeletons.
Hundreds of them. And for decades, nobody knew who they were.
This is Roopkund, five thousand metres up in Uttarakhand.
In 1942, a forest ranger found the bones as the ice melted.
scenes.label: Artist's impression

scenes.text: The first fear? Japanese soldiers from World War Two.
Wrong. These bones were far older.
Then came the legend: pilgrims killed by a deadly hailstorm.
scenes.label: Artist's impression

scenes.text: But in 2019, scientists tested their DNA, and the story broke apart.
scenes.label: Artist's impression

scenes.text: Most were Indians who died more than a thousand years ago.
But fourteen of them were different. Their DNA matched people from Greece and Crete.
And they died around 1800. A thousand years later.
scenes.label: Artist's impression

scenes.text: What were Mediterranean travellers doing on a frozen Himalayan lake?
Nobody knows. And every summer, the ice gives back a few more bones...
